text:
Logan O'Connor's season started late for the hardest of reasons. He stepped away from the Avalanche in October after his father's sudden death, and the coverage since, from a Yahoo Sports piece on how he keeps his father's memory close to Mile High Sports writing that he's back "with a heavy heart," has been about a person first and a hockey player second. We'd leave it there, with respect.

On the ice, he's settled back into the fourth line he helped define. Corey Masisak of The Denver Post noted that Parker Kelly lacked a set line while O'Connor was away, and that with his "old pal" back the fourth line is "back to business as usual." He has 3 assists in 10 games on just under 13 minutes a night, all three in his last four games, and no goals yet on 1.6 expected, which is the kind of gap that closes with time.

The undrafted Texan, a 2022 Cup winner with Colorado, missed most of last season too (13 games). Getting him back in the lineup, steady and healthy, matters to this team more than his point totals ever will.
